name: Dominican Republic
summary: A white cross dividing blue and red quarters, with the coat of arms in the centre: a shield with an open Bible, a cross and six spears and flags. It is the only national flag that shows a Bible.
origin: Juan Pablo Duarte, founder of the secret society La Trinitaria, designed the flag based on the Haitian blue and red with a white cross added. It was raised at independence from Haiti on 27 February 1844 and adopted in the constitution of 6 November 1844.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The blood shed by the heroes of independence.

symbols.name: Open Bible
symbols.description: A Bible open at John 8:32, 'And ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free'.

symbols.name: Cross
symbols.description: A small golden cross above the Bible.

symbols.name: Mottoes
symbols.description: 'DIOS, PATRIA, LIBERTAD' above and 'REPÚBLICA DOMINICANA' below.

history.label: Dominican Republic
history.note: Interrupted by Spanish annexation 1861–1865 and US occupation 1916–1924.

facts: It is the only national flag with a Bible.
The quarters alternate so that blue is at the upper hoist and lower fly.
Flag Day is 27 February, Independence Day.
clues: A white cross between blue and red quarters, with a shield holding an open book.
The only national flag that shows a Bible.
Its design added a white cross to a neighbour's colours.
